note: Revised ground+foliage palette only (DRAKANTOS_VISUAL_STUDY.md item #6) -- darker and less saturated than the forest-v4 day ramps, with saturation reserved for emissive props and small focal highlights. Derived as a documented HSV shift of forest_v4_palette.js (see renderPreset below for the exact multipliers), not new hand-picked hex, so any already-painted forest-v4/v6/v7 ground/foliage sprite or tile can be approximated with the same math without re-baking art. This file does NOT touch ambient lighting/day-night (study items #3/#7) -- that is game-dev renderer work, out of this package.

accentSaturated.note: Reserved for emissive props (data_crystal / mushroom_bioluminescent / data_totem), their point-light color (see tileset.json "light" field on each), and tiny focal sparkle pixels (puddle reflection, wet shore-stone sheen). Never applied to base ground/foliage fills -- that contrast is the point of DRAKANTOS_VISUAL_STUDY.md item #6.

renderPreset.description: How a renderer can reproduce this exact shift procedurally on an existing forest-v4/v6/v7 ground or foliage sprite/tile, instead of re-baking every asset: convert each opaque pixel to HSV, multiply saturation and value by the ground/foliage multipliers below (ground/decor/foliage layers ONLY -- never characters, UI, or this pack's own emissive props), convert back to RGB. For a flat (non-ramped) sprite, treat its lightest ~12% of pixels by value as the "rim highlight" and use the gentler rimHighlight multipliers on those instead, so sunlit edges keep reading as lit.
renderPreset.scopeNote: Apply only to ground/decor/foliage layers. Never multiply characters, UI, or this pack's emissive props/lights -- their saturation being untouched is the contrast the study asked for.
